title: Īśvarasiddhi — Proof of the Lord
author: Utpaladeva
text:
The Īśvarasiddhi is the first member of Utpaladeva's Siddhitrayi, composed in tenth-century Kashmir as the opening demonstration of the recognition school. Under an auspicious frame it sets out to establish the Lord — not by appeal to revelation but by inference from the ordinary world: bodies bespeak a conscious maker just as pots bespeak a potter. What is argued is that the ordered, meaning-bearing character of experienced things requires a consciousness that has already shaped them before any individual cognizer arrives.

Its juice: the proof turns the world's intelligibility into evidence. Every object we take for granted arrives pre-structured, and that structuring cannot come from matter or from the transient self — it points to a universal Lord who is at once the ground of things and the ultimate recognizand of the whole trilogy that follows.
